predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: Susiana, the Seleucid satrapy at the head of the Persian Gulf

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: Khuzestan: 'extinction by a Sasanian invasion in the early 3rd century AD' (page); Ardashir 'headed towards Khuzestan and killed the governor of Susa' (Ardashir I page)

ledger.x: 147 BC: Kamnaskires I Soter founds the kingdom of Elymais in Susiana.
140/139 BC: Mithridates I conquers Elymais and rules it directly.

c. 82 BC: Elymais has its own kings again after the rebellions. Elymais page: direct control lasted until about 82 BC with occasional rebellions; Kamnaskires III and Anzaze reign c. 82-62/61 BC with coins attested 82-75 BC. The year is the page's 'around 82 BC'; the restored state is a Parthian vassal, not independent.

c. 82 BC: the restored kingdom of Elymais is a Parthian vassal. Elymais page (re-read 2026-10-19): the kingdom was 'frequently a vassal under Parthian control' (intro); infobox status 'Autonomous state, frequently a vassal of the Parthian Empire'; 'From 140/139 BC, Elymais was then under direct Parthian control for…
221/222: the vassalage ends with the kingdom.
221/222: a Sasanian invasion ends the kingdom of Elymais.

wars.name: Parthian conquest of Elymais
wars.outcome: Elymais passed under direct Parthian control for several decades; Mithridates I's forces occupied Susa.

wars.name: Elymaean rebellions against Parthia
wars.outcome: Occasional rebellions until about 82 BC; then Kamnaskires III and Anzaze rule a vassal Elymais.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of Elymais
wars.outcome: Ardashir I's invasion extinguished the kingdom (221/222); the land became the Sasanian province of Khuzestan.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; Khuzestan is a reading of 'Susiana'.
